subject: physics
title: Say Cheese... It's a Conic, пункт b
statement:
You are studying the motion of charged particles constrained to the $xy$-plane. Particle $\alpha$, with charge $+1$ C, is fixed at the origin. For motion under an inverse-square central force, trajectories are conic sections with the fixed particle at a focus. In polar coordinates: for an attractive interaction (ellipse), $r = \frac{r_0}{1 + e\cos\phi}$, $e < 1$; for a repulsive interaction (hyperbola), $r = \frac{r_0}{e\cos\phi - 1}$, $e > 1$. You have a camera that takes three snapshots of a moving particle at equal time intervals.

**Пункт b.** Now particle $\beta$ is replaced by particle $\gamma$, which has charge $+2$ C and is free to move in the plane. In three consecutive snapshots, its positions are $(3\ \text{m}, -4\ \text{m})$, $(2\ \text{m}, 0)$, $(3\ \text{m}, 4\ \text{m})$. Assuming the motion is governed only by the Coulomb interaction with $\alpha$, determine the angle $\theta$ (measured from the positive $x$-axis) of the velocity of particle $\gamma$ at large times.
